LUXVAR / constructed symbolic system

Designed structure.
Testable claims.
Explicit limits.

LUXVAR is a constructed symbolic language created by Reza Nirouyar within the VARZIN Project. Its morphology and thematic organization are designed; independent semantic emergence is not assumed.

Core-30 public registry5 designed axes801-entry wider design layer
Current interpretation

Designed morphemic and structural regularities are real properties of the constructed system. Whether models or humans recover intended semantics independently is a separate empirical question.

01 / design

What LUXVAR is.

The broader design layer lists 801 entries across five intended thematic axes: Light, Reflection, Silence, Gate, and Motion. Core-30 is the public registry subset used in several tests. The wider 801-entry layer is not a claim that 801 roots are equally validated empirical items.

Designed

Morphology

Project analyses report non-random surface and morphemic structure under specified comparison procedures.

Public subset

Core-30

Thirty registered entries across five designed axes, with a historical manifest-hash prefix preserved in the record.

Boundary

Not a scientific instrument

No external field, frequency-based meaning, or non-human origin is established by the current evidence.

02 / computational record

What the tests did and did not recover.

01

Morphology and clustering

Project-reported morphology: z = 4.36, p < 0.001; silhouette = 0.406 versus shuffled mean 0.174. The reported natural cluster count was k = 3; the k = 6 Hexacore hypothesis was rejected under that analysis.

02

Phonotactic classification

GEN-001 reported 98.9% five-fold cross-validation accuracy with delta-majority +32.2% in the tested setup. GEN-003R+ reported uniqueness 0.738, 95% CI [0.703, 0.781], against six curated reference-language corpora.

03

Semantic-axis tests

SEM-001 reported no semantic-axis string signal. SEM-002 scored 1/4 against a criterion of at least 2/4; the criterion was not met.

04

Frozen model tests

Track D reported Mistral 7B ARI = −0.0337 and Llama 3 8B ARI = 0.0152 against intended axis/orbit labels. This is a negative result for those tested models under that protocol, not a universal statement about AI systems.

03 / interpretation

Structure is not the same as semantics.

Supported within scope

  • LUXVAR has intentionally designed structural regularities.
  • Specified project analyses detect non-random surface/morphemic patterns.
  • Explicit training can recover targeted labels or group position in later experiments.
  • Negative results and corrections remain part of the public record.

Not established

  • Independent semantic emergence or recovery of intended axes.
  • Universal or non-human origin.
  • Physical or consciousness-field effects.
  • Quantum mechanisms or causal frequency effects.
  • Systematic held-out composition in the tested Appendix G procedure.

Historical title note: the archived LUXVAR v2.2 title retains the phrase “AI-Recoverable” for citation continuity. The current project interpretation does not treat independent recovery of the intended semantic axes as established.
